question: After the Battle of Plassey, _______ was made Nawab of the Bengal.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mir Jafar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mir Jafar was made the Nawab of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.**
 
• The British East India Company supported Mir Jafar as Nawab because he had betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah in exchange for power.
 
• Mir Jafar became a puppet ruler under the control of the British East India Company, marking the beginning of British dominance in Bengal.
 
• His rule allowed the British to consolidate their political and economic power in India through exploitation and manipulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Siraj-ud-Daulah:** Siraj-ud-Daulah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal. He opposed the British East India Company’s growing influence in Bengal, leading to the Battle of Plassey in 1757. Betrayed by Mir Jafar during the battle, Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated and later killed.
 
• **Alivardi Khan:** Alivardi Khan was the Nawab of Bengal before Siraj-ud-Daulah and ruled from 1740 to 1756. His reign was marked by constant warfare against the Marathas and internal consolidation of power. He was Siraj-ud-Daulah’s maternal grandfather.
 
• **Mir Kasim:** Mir Kasim succeeded Mir Jafar as the Nawab of Bengal in 1760 after the British removed Mir Jafar for failing to meet their expectations. Mir Kasim attempted to reassert his independence but was defeated by the British in the Battle of Buxar in 1764.
 
• **The Battle of Plassey:** Fought on June 23, 1757, the Battle of Plassey marked the beginning of British rule in India. The British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah with the help of Mir Jafar’s betrayal. This battle was pivotal in establishing British dominance over Bengal.
